item.title: 76ers reportedly make NBA history with never before seen prediction market partnership
item.description: 76ers reportedly make NBA history with never before seen prediction market partnership originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers signed LeBron James for just $8 million this summer, marking the largest pay cut in NBA history. Sure, James has made plenty of money throughout his career since joining the NBA, so the contract wasn't necessarily a big deal for him. However, James found another way to make money through endorsements and partnerships, including one with Polymarket. “LeBron James will make more money from his Polymarket partnership than from playing for the 76ers, Front Office Sports has learned. The prediction-market platform is paying James $15 million a year under the recently announced partnership, sources tell FOS. James is not an investor in Polymarket, just an endorser, one source says," Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel and Ben Horney wrote. James was smart to pursue this opportunity, as it gives him another source of income outside of his playing contract. However, NBA insider Brett Siegel revealed that this type of arrangement could become a trend for players signing smaller deals. “As far as my knowledge goes, this doesn't interfere with any CBA rules, but moving forward, these side deals players have with companies could directly lead to smaller contracts to help with cap relief, which in theory, is kind of like cap circumvention," Siegel wrote. On Friday, The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov revealed that the 76ers organization would be partnering with Kalshi, marking the first time an NBA team has made a prediction market platform its official partner. “The Philadelphia 76ers have struck a multi-year deal with Kalshi to make Kalshi its official prediction market partner. Sixers say they're the 1st NBA team to name an official prediction market partner, and are following in the footsteps of the NBA's deals this week,” Vorkunov wrote. The game is continuing to grow off the court, and deals like this were unheard of just a couple of seasons ago. It is certainly something new, but other teams will likely start pursuing similar partnerships. In a season where James could have set a trend with prediction markets, his team in Philadelphia may be doing the same. Perhaps James was the inspiration the 76ers needed to pursue this deal with Kalshi. item.title: Zverev thrashes GB's Fery to reach Vienna semis
item.description: Alexander Zverev won the French Open and US Open this year [Getty Images] Alexander Zverev marked his rise to world number one with a dominant victory over Britain's Arthur Fery to reach the semi-finals of the Vienna Open. The German top seed, who is set to replace Jannik Sinner at the summit of the men's rankings, needed just 58 minutes to secure a comprehensive 6-0 6-2 win. Fery did not look at his best throughout the encounter after receiving treatment on his leg near the end of his last-16 win over Lorenzo Musetti on Thursday. The match was a repeat of the pair's Wimbledon semi-final this summer, which Zverev won in straight sets to end Fery's remarkable run. "I think Arthur is a bit of a different opponent than I had yesterday. He doesn't have the same firepower, but he plays tactically extremely well," said Zverev. "I know the score was 6-0 6-2, but he should not put himself down too much. It is his first year on the Tour and he is doing amazing things." Like at Wimbledon, Fery upset the odds to reach the last eight in Vienna by beating former world number five Musetti, but the 24-year-old was outclassed by Zverev. Zverev dropped only six points on serve in the match, while bringing up nine break points against Fery, converting five of them. The German is aiming for his third title this year after winning the French Open and US Open. He has taken advantage of injuries to Carlos Alcaraz and Sinner this year to leapfrog them in the rankings, becoming the second German to reach the top of the men's game after Boris Becker in 1991. Zverev will face Australian fifth seed Alex de Minaur or Italy's Matteo Berrettini in the last four. In the other semi-final, Spanish second seed Alcaraz will face Russian third seed Daniil Medvedev. Seven-time Grand Slam-winner Alcaraz beat American seventh seed Tommy Paul 6-4 7-6 (7-2) in his quarter-final. Medvedev triumphed over France's Adrian Mannarino 6-2 6-3 in his last-eight tie - a victory which seals the 30-year-old's place in the season-ending ATP Finals. It will be Medvedev's seventh time appearing at the finals as he joins the already-qualified Zverev, Alcaraz and Ben Shelton. At the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo, world number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from her quarter-final tie against Leylah Fernandez with a neck injury. Rybakina's withdrawal comes one day after she secured the year-end women's singles number one ranking . Fernandez, who received a walkover, will face Russia's Kamilla Rakhimova in the last-four. item.title: Arsenal dealt multiple injury boosts ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Arsenal dealt multiple injury boosts ahead of Liverpool clash Arsenal Injury Update Before Liverpool Clash as Rice, Calafiori and Tzolis Return to Training Arsenal head to Anfield with a useful boost, even if the broader picture still carries a few complications. Ahead of the Premier League meeting with Liverpool, Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Declan Rice, Christos Tzolis and Riccardo Calafiori all returned to training on Friday. That matters, because Arsenal need a reaction and they need bodies. The timing is obvious. Arsenal are coming off an embarrassing Carabao Cup exit, dumped out by Fleetwood Town after a 1-1 draw and a 5-3 defeat on penalties. Aaron Loupalo-Bi scored before the break, Viktor Gyokeres levelled in the second half, and Jay Lynch did the rest with a string of saves. The result put Arsenal in the wrong kind of history, the first reigning Premier League champions to lose a League Cup tie against a fourth-tier side. Arsenal Injury Update Ahead of Anfield Still, league form has been solid. Arsenal sit second on 21 points, level with Manchester City and behind only on goal difference. They have conceded just five goals in eight league games, and the 2-0 win over Everton last weekend underlined that they remain organised, efficient and hard to break down. That is why the fitness update matters. Rice, Calafiori and Tzolis being back in training gives Arteta options in midfield, defence and attack. Noni Madueke remains uncertain and will be checked again after Saturday’s session. Photo: IMAGO Liverpool vs Arsenal Carries Weight for Both Sides Liverpool, now led by Andoni Iraola, are fourth on 15 points and already six behind Arsenal. At home, that gap is the story. Win, and the table tightens. Lose, and Arsenal gain control over a direct rival near the top end. There are still absentees for the visitors. Bukayo Saka is expected to miss at least six weeks with a quad injury suffered against Bayern Munich. William Saliba has not featured at all this season because of a long-term back issue. Max Dowman is also out after Arsenal failed in their appeal against his red card at Fleetwood, meaning a three-match suspension that also rules him out against Hull City and Newcastle United. Premier League Table Adds Edge at Anfield So Arsenal arrive stronger than they looked a few days ago, but not whole. That is usually enough to shape a big away game. At Anfield, availability often tells its own story.

item.title: Browns fans weigh in on last week’s offensive outburst, and is Cleveland the best team in the AFC?
item.description: The Browns had yet another game-winning drive against the Titans last week, their fifth to correspond with five victories — to improve to 5-2 on the season. Week-to-week, fan confidence increased by 3 percentage points up to 88%, a new season high again. If Cleveland can sweep the Steelers this week, that percentage might shoot up into the 90s. By comparison, 70% of Steelers fans are confident in the direction of their team. Browns fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Browns polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Dawgs By Nature fans. Then discuss the results with the Dawg Pound. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Besides the confidence meter, the main question we asked this week was focused on what fans felt about the Browns’ offensive outburst last week. Was it a sign that they’ve turned the corner? A fluke? Overall, 51% said that the offense was nice, but attributed much of it to the Titans just sucking. 47% of fans think the offense had indeed turned a corner, while only 2% think it was just a fluke what happened last week. One fan thinks Todd Monken is opening up the offense, but needs to keep at it and break some more tendencies: I feel like Monken is opening up the offense. I think he was going tight too often. I love TIGHT formations, but with a young line and mediocre FB/blocking TEs, I question the fetish. I hope they just dont’ settle. mix it up. go tight every now and then. make the defense rotate their personnel, and just smash them when we have a mismatch. I just hate going TIGHT, after TIGHT, after TIGHT. the defense just gets bigger, bigger and bigger. I keep saying. the defense has the advantage, and if we’re predictable getting even 2 yards into their territory is tough. speed is key. SPREAD EM WIDE!! Corley and Wallace are said to be blocking well. let’s not be too predictable. they have speed too. get them out in space, especially when PIT (or anyone else) isn’t looking for it. 1 target for the whole year on 116 snaps. that’s just not right. Another fan thinks it’s really a combination of things coming together: I think it’s a combination of the Titans suck and we are finding a groove. The offense is going to to get better. You have a lot of young guys out there and a new O-line that is starting to play better together. There are going to be bumps in the road, but this team is improving. On a national scale, fans were asked who the best team in the AFC is, and the Browns actually received 5% of the vote. Don’t shoot the messenger. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3.5 point underdogs against the Steelers this week, with the over/under being 39.5.

item.title: Alex Afari Jr. receives positive ruling in eligibility lawsuit
item.description: The NCAA’s fight to keep Kentucky linebacker Alex Afari Jr. and other athletes off the field took a hit Friday when Kentucky Court of Appeals Judge Sara Walter Combs denied the organization’s request for emergency relief. More than 30 athletes from the class of 2022 are named in the ongoing lawsuit, and they will continue to exhaust every option in pursuit of an additional year of eligibility in their respective sports. As things stand Friday afternoon, the athletes in the lawsuit, including Afari, are eligible to play. Does this mean it’s over and the litigation is finished? Not quite, but we may be nearing a final resolution. Eligibility could change again, because the next step is for a three-judge panel of the Kentucky Court of Appeals to consider the NCAA’s request for interlocutory relief. The athletes’ attorneys have until Nov. 6 to respond to that motion. The situation is one thing for basketball players still navigating the eligibility waters. For players like Afari, though, the college football season is winding down and time is running out. Thankfully, the Cincinnati native has seen the field in spurts this season despite the back-and-forth court rulings. Afari has played in six of UK’s eight games and recorded 11 total tackles, but he hasn’t had the chance to shine the way we’ve seen in previous seasons. For the Kentucky Football program, this has been no normal season by any stretch of the imagination. With all sights set on making and advancing in the College Football Playoff, having depth pieces like Alex Afari Jr. at your disposal will be huge for Will Stein and his staff. You also have to feel for him and the other athletes named in the lawsuit, as they want some finality in this situation as much as any of us do. It seems like that final decision may be coming sooner rather than later.

item.title: What Does Max Verstappen Make of a Le Mans Drive With Daniel Ricciardo?
item.description: Max Verstappen has responded to Daniel Ricciardo’s query about a potential Le Mans 24 Hours stint. In the build-up to the F1 Mexico GP weekend, the Beyond the Grid podcast featured Ricciardo in the hot seat for the first time, opening up about life after Formula 1 and the dreaded end in Singapore. It left him humiliated, and he explained why . The Australian certainly wants to return, but probably for a one-off race like the Le Mans 24 Hours rather than anything else, to find closure on his terms. He is not ready for anything full-time as he is already burned out from racing. But a one-off, sharing data and everything with a proper teammate, would perk him up. Who can be his teammates, though? Sergio Perez popped up as a popular pairing of Red Bull ’s Verstappen and Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso, which Ricciardo is up for as well. Ricciardo Names His Potential Le Mans Teammates He does put Verstappen on his list and the second one could be Sebastian Vettel if he is up for it. “On the racing front, like, yeah, that’s something that a year ago, I would have said, ‘I will never put a helmet on again, I am done, that’s it,’” said Ricciardo. “But there’s something there; I am like, it’d be nice to also for me to, I guess, like, finish a racing career a bit more on my terms. “So, to do something, when I take the helmet off, I am smiling and happy, and maybe that’s the last bit of closure I need. I mean, the thought of doing a full championship or something just still doesn’t really sound that exciting. Probably a one-off, like a one-off Le Mans 24 Hours. “[With Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso] that seems like a popular choice. I feel he doesn’t have to; I don’t want to put pressure on him, but no, obviously Max is the name that would be high on the list. Actually, him winning in car number three made me feel a certain way, in a good way. “I’ll say Max is one that could, yeah, we talked about Red Bull, obviously, in 2018 and what if. I was trying to get back to the team at the end of my career, so maybe that’s a way that we could, yeah, give the people what they want,” summed up Ricciardo, who had been teammates with Verstappen until the 2018 F1 season. Daniel Ricciardo speaks to Calum Nicholas on the Indeed Stage at Red Bull Race Nights in Austin, Texas, USA on October 23, 2026. // Angela Wang / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610250667 // Usage for editorial use only // Verstappen Says Ricciardo is Smart to Choose Him But is Verstappen up for it? The Dutchman was asked about it during his media session at the F1 Mexico GP. The four-time champion joked about Ricciardo being a smart man to choose him. But he ruled himself out for the time being due to lack of time, with involvement in Formula 1 and also GT racing. “He’s a smart man to choose me in the car, but we have to see,” said Verstappen. “It just depends on a lot of things. Also, for me, like, if I want to do it, I want to do it properly with really good prep, and at the moment I cannot do that.

item.title: Kings rumors: Sacramento is most embarrassing team in NBA. Is Doug Christie on hot seat?
item.description: © Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Kings rumors: Sacramento is most embarrassing team in NBA. Is Doug Christie on hot seat? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sacramento Kings have endured a disastrous start to the 2026-27 NBA season, dropping their first five games by an average margin of 16.6 points. However, head coach Doug Christie is reportedly not on the hot seat despite the team’s continued struggles. According to The Athletic’s Sam Amick, Sacramento’s front office believes Christie deserves a fair opportunity to prove himself with a healthier roster before evaluating his future with the organization. Amick reported that the Kings are prioritizing the development of Christie and their younger players rather than making an immediate coaching change. However, continued losses could eventually force the organization to reconsider its position. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sacramento’s struggles reached another low Thursday night following a 132-120 loss to the previously winless New Orleans Pelicans . The defeat dropped the Kings to 0-5, with three of their losses coming by double digits. The Kings have also suffered blowout losses to the Los Angeles Clippers and San Antonio Spurs by 25 and 27 points, respectively. Kings’ injury concerns complicate Doug Christie’s future Sacramento has navigated significant injuries throughout the opening weeks of the season, with Ben Simmons, Keegan Murray, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell all sidelined. Simmons will miss the entire 2026-27 season after suffering a torn right Achilles tendon, while Murray is dealing with left ankle capsulitis. Raynaud remains sidelined with a right patellar subluxation, and Cardwell is recovering from a left calf strain. Murray is expected to be reevaluated within 10 to 14 days, while Raynaud continues his rehabilitation and Cardwell is expected to undergo another evaluation. Despite the injuries, Sacramento has received encouraging production from rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr., who recorded 34 points, 14 assists and six rebounds against New Orleans. Acuff is averaging 24.0 points and 6.6 assists through five games, providing one of the few bright spots amid Sacramento’s winless start. Christie remains in the final guaranteed season of his contract, which includes a team option for the following campaign. His immediate future appears secure, but Sacramento’s continued struggles could increase pressure on the organization to make changes. The Kings will look for their first victory Saturday when they visit the undefeated Memphis Grizzlies (5-0) at 5 p.m. PT. item.title: UTSA Basketball Coach Who Passed Out in Car Moments Before DWI Arrest Suspended Ahead of Season Start
item.description: Austin Claunch Credit: Andrew Wevers/Getty NEED TO KNOW UTSA has suspended its basketball coach after he was arrested on suspicion of driving while intoxicated Austin Claunch was arrested in Corpus Christi, Texas on Tuesday, Oct. 27 University officials said they would determine the next steps of his suspension Just days before the season opener, the University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA) has suspended basketball coach Austin Claunch following his arrest on suspicion of driving while intoxicated. Claunch, 36, was arrested in Corpus Christi just before 2 a.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 27 after police found that he performed poorly on sobriety tests, San Antonio ABC affiliate KSAT-TV reported . The coach was found passed out inside his running Mercedes, which was parked outside a gas station, according to the news station. Police noted his slurred speech and smelled alcohol on his breath, a report obtained by the outlet said. Claunch, who was identified as James Austin Claunch in the report, was taken to a hospital where his blood was drawn after he refused to take a breath test. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! On Wednesday, the university announced that it had suspended the third-year coach and will determine the next steps after reviewing the circumstances of his arrest. Austin Claunch Credit: Jason Clark/Getty “UTSA Head Men’s Basketball Coach Austin Claunch has been suspended effective today following his arrest on suspicion of driving while intoxicated,” UTSA Athletics Director Lisa Campos said in a statement Wednesday night . “The university is reviewing the circumstances and will determine appropriate next steps, including the length of his suspension.” Claunch was the youngest head coach in Division I basketball from 2018 to 2021 after he took over at Nicholls State University. He was previously an assistant coach at George Mason, Clemson, and at Alabama under Nate Oats. In a statement, Claunch took responsibility for his actions. “I made a grave error in judgment, and I deeply regret my actions and the disappointment I have caused,” Claunch said. “I sincerely apologize to the young men I have the privilege of coaching, my fellow coaches and colleagues, President [Taylor] Eighmy, Dr. Lisa Campos and the entire Roadrunner community.” Assistant Nick Bowman will serve as acting coach when the Roadrunners open the season on Monday, Nov. 2 at San Jose State. item.description: Utah Utes wide receiver Ryan Davis (9) spins away from Cincinnati Bearcats safety Christian Harrison (5) as Utah and Cincinnati play at Rice Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News No. 6 Utah (7-0, 4-0) at Cincinnati (5-2, 2-2) Kickoff: Saturday, 1:45 p.m. MDT Venue: Nippert Stadium TV: ESPN Livestream: ESPN app with participating TV provider Radio: ESPN 700 AM/92.1 FM /KZNS 1280 Series: Utah leads 1-0 Weather: Saturday’s Cincinnati forecast is high 60s through the entire game The trends For Utah: The Utes are the final Big 12 team that remains unbeaten. To achieve this status, Utah defeated previously No. 14-ranked Houston, the first opponent with a winning record the Utes have faced so far this season. The win vaulted Utah in the rankings as the team travels to Cincinnati. There is not a lot of history between the two schools, in fact, this is just the second meeting. The first meeting came in 2025 when Brendan Sorsby made the trip to Salt Lake City and left with a 45-14 thumping. For Cincinnati: Beginning the season 4-0, the Bearcats got to a strong start against weaker competition before experiencing a two-game losing streak at Arizona and West Virginia; however, Cincinnati bounced back in a big way with a win against then No. 8 Texas Tech and look to keep momentum rolling come Saturday. What to watch for This could be a tricky game for Utah as the team heads to the same venue another top-10 team traveled to and lost in the Bearcats’ game previous to this one. The Utes are coming off their biggest win so far in the season and will need to be prepared for a Cincinnati team that has a lot of momentum after a big win. The Bearcats are looking for a second straight top-10 victory on Saturday. For the Utes to return to Salt Lake City unscathed Devon Dampier (and whoever else is taking snaps) will need to take care of the football. Cincinnati turned the Red Raiders over twice along with a dominant 21-0 second quarter that ultimately led to their demise. After Utah’s game against Houston, it appears Utah has the defense to stop any offensive dominance from Cincinnati, but taking care of the football could be difficult. Throwing two interceptions against the Cougars, Dampier cannot get lackadaisical with the football or a Cincinnati home crowd could get rowdy and make things difficult. On the defensive side, the run game will be an area of focus for Morgan Scalley’s Utes. Cincinnati only had 172 yards passing in its rout of Texas Tech, but gained 255 yards on the ground against a talented Red Raiders defense. Running back Cole Tabb, coming off a 173-yard game, will be a player the Utes’ defensive game plan will take into account. And if Utah is able to create pressure on Bearcat quarterback JC French IV, the Utes could create some turnovers. item.title: Jeffery Simmons is a ‘red-level’ defender that Super Bowl teams need
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Indianapolis Colts during the third quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images What do Leonard Williams, Jalen Carter, Chris Jones, Fletcher Cox, and Aaron Donald all have in common? They’re all difference-making, All-Pro-level interior defenders who won Super Bowls. The Chicago Bears believe they just acquired one who can help them get there. At his press conference earlier today, Bears general manager Ryan Poles was asked what the trade for Jeffery Simmons means to him after a “five-year journey” to get the position right. “Yeah, you probably go all the way back to the first free agency when I took a shot there,” Poles said about his signing of Larry Ogunjobi, who failed his physical and had the contract rescinded. “I remember having conversations with you guys, and I hear it all the time; it’s like, ‘Does Poles see value in offensive linemen and defensive linemen?’ I’m well aware of the impact that those guys have on football teams,” he said. “If you do the research, you know, Super Bowl teams, really, probably you go back to 2018; since then, they all have what we call a red-level interior defensive lineman. So in order to get to there, you need one. I really believe that.” “So we’ve been searching, but the draft, again, when you go best available, sometimes the draft doesn’t provide that to you. Sometimes I know free agency really doesn’t do that at that level. It’s very hard for guys to get out of the building when they have all of those things that we’re talking about. So, we’ve been searching.” The 29-year-old Simmons has 4 Pro Bowl nods and has been named to 3 All-Pro Teams. “It was an opportunity that we had to jump on,” Poles said af the chance to trade for Simmons. “I’ve talked to you guys before in a lot of different situations. We’re going to stay opportunistic. We’re going to stay flexible. If something presents itself, we’ll see how does this fit, and this is one that we felt like we could make work. And again, it’s going to help us short-term and long-term.” Simmons is at practice today, and he’s scheduled to meet the media after. Getting right to work 💪 pic.twitter.com/iuu9xTjHS9 — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 30, 2026 Poles said it was up to the coaches if Simmons will play this week. The Bears will have one more regular practice tomorrow and have a walk-through before playing the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen held a pre-practice presser and said , “The more he (Simmons) can digest, the more opportunities there will be for him on the field. This will be a work in progress.” My guess is he’ll make his Chicago Bears debut under the lights in Seattle.

item.title: Rusev Denies Rumor About Joining New WWE Faction: 4 Alternative Ideas For His Return
item.description: WWE Rusev is healthy and ready to return to WWE television, but he is not on board with a rumor about his future. Speaking on TMZ’s Inside the Ring, Rusev was asked about a report that WWE plans to put him in a stable with Ethan Page and Big Cass . He said nobody in WWE has told him about it, and he is not sure he would want it. “It’s very internet booking. We have one, two, three bad guys, let’s put them together. I have not heard anything about this, but also, I don’t know if I’m okay with that either,” Rusev said. “Like, that guy, I left for a couple of months. I got hurt, sickness, and all that. So Page just went out there and found another tall guy to back him up. Like, ‘F you, bro. You never called me, checked on me. You’re just gonna go and find yourself a big guy? Good for you. I don’t wanna be associated with that.'” Rusev did leave room for the report to have been true at some point. “Also, because someone said that they could have been greenlit on Tuesday, but by the time Wednesday night comes, everything could be scrapped. Everything is changing by the hour and day,” he said. item.title: Rangers captain plays Tinker Bell at Halloween party: ‘makes group closer’
item.description: At 6-foot-1, nearly 220 pounds, and with a smile that features some chipped chicklets, J.T. Miller is not soon to be confused with Tinker Bell. But indeed, the New York Rangers captain rose to the occasion at the players’ annual Halloween party earlier in the week dressed as the famed Disney character. “It was a lot of fun,” Miller said Friday after the Rangers returned to practice following two days away from the rink. “My wife picks out partner costumes where I’m the woman and she’s the guy … and this year I was Tinker Bell and she was Peter Pan. “I’m sure there are [pictures]. I didn’t take any, but I’m sure there are some out there.” Miller probably does his fair share of dressing up at home, where he and his wife Natalie are raising two daughters — eight-year-old Scotlyn and seven-year-old Scarlett — and son Owen, who is four. But the 33-year-old had no hesitation being the belle of the ball Tuesday when the Rangers gathered with their families for a fun night amidst a busy first month of the 2026-27 NHL season. “I just think it makes the group closer,” Miller said about the team get together. Following their 6-3 loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Monday, the Rangers were one of only two teams to have played 14 games already this season. And it appeared to be catching up with them, since they hit a five-day break in the schedule on a three-game losing streak and just 1-4-1 in their past six. “I think this was a great time to have [a get together], plenty of time between games, some days off in there,” Miller explained. “A little, down, I would say, with our record the last couple of weeks, so I think it was good to have a little fun and get away from it, re-energize, and it makes you excited to come to work on days like today. We all had a lot of fun as group with the wives and girlfriends. It was a great time.” Defenseman Sean Durzi was impressed with the creative costumes on display at the party, including one couple who came dressed as the Statue of Liberty and a tourist. But which Rangers player had the best costume? “I think Scotty Morrow won,” Miller offered. “His was really good. I don’t want to say what he was, but he did great.” The Rangers practice again Saturday and then are back in game action Sunday, when they host the Edmonton Oilers at Madison Square Garden. item.title: A.J. Brown Injury Report Sparks “Washed” Talk From Fans
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images Fans are calling A.J. Brown “washed” after he missed another practice session. Yahoo Sports reported the wide receiver was added to the injury report on Wednesday with a knee ailment. He sat out Thursday’s practice with the New England Patriots. This is not the first time his health has been a major worry this season. Brown has missed four games already due to injury. He was activated on Oct. 17 and played in the last two contests. But his production remains low. With only three games played, the receiver who has made the Pro Bowl three times secured nine receptions totaling 101 yards without scoring a touchdown. The high ankle sprain he suffered in the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks cost him a month of football. A knee issue has raised concern for the team. Fans Call Him “Made of Glass” People are saying the trade from Philadelphia was a mistake. According to Yahoo Sports, New England acquired him from the Eagles in exchange for a fifth-round pick in 2027 and a first-round pick in 2028. That deal looked like a win for the Patriots on paper. Now, the physical toll seems to be catching up to him. Some fans are even claiming “He Is Made of Glass,” according to the headlines surfacing on Yahoo Sports. Some observers are questioning the player’s value. The phrase “Eagles Fleeced Patriots” is trending online. It suggests New England got the short end of the stick. The team expected a star who could carry the offense. Instead, they have a player who cannot stay on the field. Nine catches in three games is not enough to justify a first-round pick in the trade. Coach Downing Still Has Faith Despite the noise, the coaching staff is trying to stay calm. WR coach Todd Downing spoke to the media on Thursday. He said he still has faith in the wide receiver. item.title: Pep who? Maresca claims reborn City are ahead of schedule after summer upheaval
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-MANCHESTER CITY-TRAINING - AFP Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca believes the club is ahead of schedule following major summer changes after Pep Guardiola's decade of dominance. Maresca expressed satisfaction as City sit top of the Premier League despite significant squad changes. Maresca leads Manchester City transition smoothly Manchester City sit top of the Premier League table after eight matches under new manager Enzo Maresca. The Italian took charge following a trophy-laden decade under Pep Guardiola, navigating major squad departures including Bernardo Silva, John Stones, and Rodri. City remain active on all fronts, reaching the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup and securing two wins from three Champions League ties. Maresca believes the club's rebuild is progressing faster than initially anticipated. Maresca insists City are competing ahead of schedule Speaking ahead of Saturday's fixture against Brighton, Maresca highlighted the speed of the team's adaptation. "I think we’re going in the right direction," Maresca affirmed. "I said in the last press conference, after so many years to change manager and many players it takes time to compete again and in this moment we are competing." "We changed many players and the manager but good thing about the club is we are competing in all the competitions and we know it takes time when you make this many changes but in this moment, we continue in the same way," he added. Manager embraces Premier League unpredictability Maresca acknowledged that competitive parity across the English top flight makes maintaining consistency a constant challenge. The manager pointed to teams like Aston Villa, Newcastle, and third-placed Brighton as proof of the league's rising standards. "Every season you can have one or two surprises that they are there and now the level is so similar that you can drop points against any team and win against any team," Maresca noted. City aim to solidify summit position Manchester City prepare to host high-flying Brighton at the Etihad Stadium in Saturday's 15:00 UK kick-off. Maresca's side look to secure three points before turning attention to European duties against RB Leipzig. City continue their campaign aiming to preserve momentum across all competitions.

item.description: Olympic athletes from Russia celebrate after winning the men's gold medal hockey game against Germany, 4-3, in overtime at the 2018 Winter Olympics, Sunday, Feb. 25, 2018, in Gangneung, South Korea. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong) | Jae C. Hong For decades, Russia has been among the top teams in international hockey — right up there with Canada, the United States and Sweden. After the country’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, the International Ice Hockey Federation barred Russia from competing in any of the federation’s events, including the Olympics, the World Championships, the World Juniors and other significant tournaments. On Friday, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Russia must be allowed to participate in five IIHF events, effective immediately: 2027 Men’s World Championship 2027 Women’s World Championship 2027 Men’s World Junior Championship 2027 U18 Men’s World Championship 2027 U18 Women’s World Championship A major factor in the decision was the lack of evidence to support the IIHF’s security concerns, according to AP . The decision does not impact the 2030 men’s or women’s Olympic tournaments, though they are governed by the IIHF. The International Olympic Committee did, however, lift the ban on Russian athletes in July, meaning that opens the door for them to compete in the 2028 Summer Games in Los Angeles. Given the rulings of both the IOC and the CAS, it’s possible that Russian hockey players could be allowed to compete in Alpes 2030. One major concern that kept the IIHF from allowing Russia to compete was the possibility of other countries backing out in response. A number of national hockey governing bodies have released statements regarding the decision. All expressed disappointment. Finland said it will not restrict its athletes from participating, while Germany, Czechia and Austria said they will take time to make their decisions. Hockey Canada has not released an official statement, though it told Sportsnet that it is “seeking clarity” on the decision. The men’s World Junior Championship takes place in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta beginning Dec. 26. Similarly, the Swedish Ice Hockey Association has not released a statement, though its president, Anders Larsson, told Swedish News agency TT that “a boycott is not on the table.” As of the time of writing, USA Hockey has not released a statement.
